title: Median of two sorted sensor logs
prompt:
Two sensors produce sorted logs a and b; return the median of all readings combined in O(log(min(m, n))) time, without merging the logs.

- a and b each have 0 to 100,000 integers between -10^6 and 10^6, sorted in nondecreasing order; together they have at least one reading.
- For an odd total, return the middle reading. For an even total, return the mean of the two middle readings, which may end in .5 (for example 2.5).
hints: Merging is O(m + n). Think of cutting both logs so the left pieces together hold half the readings.
If you take i readings from the shorter log a, you must take j = half - i from b. Binary search on i.
A cut is right when a[i - 1] <= b[j] and b[j - 1] <= a[i] (treat missing sides as -infinity / +infinity). Then the median comes from the max of the left sides and the min of the right sides.

solution.explanation: The median splits the combined readings into a left half and a right half. Choosing i elements from the shorter log fixes j = half - i from the other, and the split is valid exactly when both left maxima are <= both right minima. Binary search on i moves left when a's left part is too big and right when b's is, so it finishes in O(log(min(m, n))) steps.

complexity.notes: Binary searching the shorter log keeps j in range and gives the log(min) bound.

followUps: Return the k-th smallest reading of the two logs instead.
Generalise to the median of k sorted logs. What is the best complexity you can get?
